title: Hedge Funds and the Treasury Cash-Futures Disconnect
about: Leveraged Treasury cash-futures basis trading and liquidity stress.
findings: Authors document basis positions and unwinds; interpret March2020 unwind largely as a consequence, rather than primary cause, of stress.
mechanism: Convergence across deliverable cash bonds, financing and futures may compensate arbitrageurs; not an outright ZN direction signal.
build_on: Supporting risk/accounting reference. Coupon cashflows, repo, deliverable baskets and native contracts are material, unowned legs.
can_strategy_code_be_made: A cash-futures ledger needs those exact inputs and funding constraints; continuous ZN alone cannot replicate it.
reading_scope: OFR102-page PDF abstract/introduction and CTD/convergence sections PDF pp13–15 selected; not a full review.
owned_input_mapping: ZN minutes are one leg; security-level CTD/coupons/conversion factors/repo and regulatory positions are not supplied.
summary: Supporting risk/accounting reference. Coupon cashflows, repo, deliverable baskets and native contracts are material, unowned legs.
deeper_investigation: Park unless genuinely new matching source/input availability or a novel executable mechanism appears; continue distinct owned-compatible discovery.
